title: The Jellyfish That Reverses Aging
description:
There's a real jellyfish species that, instead of dying of old age, can turn back into an earlier version of itself and start its life cycle over.

#shorts #sciencefacts #jellyfish #didyouknow

scenes.text: There's a jellyfish that, instead of dying of old age, can turn back into a baby version of itself and start its life over.
It's called Turritopsis dohrnii, barely 4.5 millimeters across -- smaller than your pinky nail.
When it's injured, starving, or under stress, its fully grown adult cells actually transform back into an earlier form, through a process called transdifferentiation.
It's the biological equivalent of a butterfly reverting back into a caterpillar, cell by cell.

Theoretically, it can repeat this cycle forever, which is why scientists call it biologically immortal. It can still die -- eaten, diseased, injured beyond repair -- it just doesn't die of old age the way almost everything else does.
It was first noticed doing this in 1988, by a student studying jellyfish in the Mediterranean. It's since spread to oceans worldwide, likely hitching rides in the ballast water of cargo ships.
If you could reset your own age every time things got hard, would you actually want to?
